passage:
A cemetery added small codes to some tombstones. Visitors could scan them to read life stories, see photos, or hear family recordings.
Some families liked the idea. Others felt a grave should remain quiet and simple.
The cemetery allowed families to choose.
A student visiting with his grandmother scanned one code and heard a man singing a song from his youth. The student felt surprised by how alive the memory seemed.
The digital tombstone raised questions about grief, privacy, and memory.
Technology can extend remembrance, but it should not force one style of mourning on everyone. Even memory needs consent.
